title: Oasis Documentary ‘Don’t Look Back In Anger’ Gets First Trailer: Watch
summary: Steven Knight’s new film hits theaters on Sept. 11.
contentText:
Oasis fans are getting their first look at the band’s upcoming reunion documentary.

On Saturday (July 4), Oasis unveiled the first official trailer for Don’t Look Back In Anger , the upcoming documentary chronicling Liam and Noel Gallagher’s long-awaited reunion and the band’s blockbuster Live ’25 comeback tour.

“Get ready to experience one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. Witness the return of Oasis in Don’t Look Back In Anger , in cinemas and IMAX this September,” Walt Disney Studios captioned a joint Instagram post featuring the teaser.

The 45-second trailer opens with explosive audience footage from the Oasis Live ’25 Tour, which launched in Cardiff, Wales, on July 4, 2025, and concluded in São Paulo, Brazil, on Nov. 23, 2025.

The stadium trek — the Gallagher brothers’ first live performances together since Oasis split in 2009 — spanned 41 shows across the U.K., Europe, North America and South America.

From there, Noel is heard saying, “I just don’t see myself on stage with Liam. I just don’t see it,” as the trailer cuts to behind-the-scenes footage of the band preparing for rehearsals.

“The way it finished… unacceptable,” Liam adds.

The brothers’ skeptical expressions appear as a reporter says, “Most thought it would never happen. And some still aren’t convinced.”

Soundtracked by Oasis’ 1995 classic “Morning Glory,” the teaser flashes the words, “The great wait is over. Experience the return of Oasis,” alongside footage of Noel and Liam performing throughout the reunion tour.

The preview ends with Liam declaring, “It’s gonna be chaos.”

Don’t Look Back In Anger — named after Oasis’ 1996 anthem, which reached the top 10 on Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart — will arrive in theaters and select IMAX cinemas on Sept. 11 before streaming globally later this year on Disney+ and Hulu in the United States.

Produced in partnership with Disney, Magna Studios and Sony Music Vision, the film follows Oasis’ successful Live ’25 reunion tour, the band’s first run of concerts in 16 years. Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight serves as executive producer, while Shut Up and Play the Hits and Meet Me in the Bathroom filmmakers Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace direct.

The studios previously revealed that the documentary will feature rehearsal and backstage footage, along with Noel and Liam Gallagher’s first joint interview in 25 years. It will also explore “the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what [its] music means to audiences and generations worldwide,” according to a press statement.
